I've been working this land for 40 years. I know every corner of it. My land is 10.1 mu, and I do what my father did and what I've always done — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same land, same rotation. It works. I don't change what works.

**Wheat (October planting):** I'll plough the field first — I always plough before wheat, it breaks up the maize stubble and loosens the soil properly. I'll use the improved seed variety I've been buying from the township supply station for years — good germination, local adaptation. I'm not going to try something new at my age. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting and then add urea at jointing stage, same as always. My well lets me water three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. That's enough. I'll spray once for weeds in spring and once for rust and aphids. Expecting around 450 jin per mu — that's what I usually get.

**Maize (June planting, right after wheat harvest):** I won't till before maize. Too much work and the soil is still loose from the wheat season. I'll direct-sow the hybrid seed —郑单958 type, everyone around here uses it, gives good cobs. I apply more nitrogen for maize than wheat, maize is hungry. Two irrigations: one when it's dry at the big bell stage, one at silking if needed. Two pesticide passes — one for armyworm, one late season. Expect around 550 jin per mu.

Seven mouths to feed, and I sell the surplus to the grain station. This plan feeds us and puts something aside.
